subject: Request: DPA addendum for ML custody, subprocessor attestations, and model-improvement opt-out
messages:
From: Anna Patel <anna.legal@zenhealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-29T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: DPA addendum request: ML model improvement & subprocessor attestations

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the onboarding call yesterday. Our legal and procurement teams reviewed Redwood's standard DPA and we have two remaining asks we need addressed before procurement can sign:

1) A DPA addendum or schedule that explicitly states our data will not be used to improve or retrain models (no-model-improvement / no-train). We need operational detail or an attestation that our interactions won't be included in model updates.

2) A current list of subprocessors and a signed attestation template confirming they will not use ZenHealth data for model improvement and that any transfers will meet our onshore residency requirements (US-only).

I've attached a redline of the DPA with comments (Zen_DPA_Redline_v3.pdf). Our procurement timeline is tight — would you be able to provide a proposed addendum and the attestation template by close of business Wednesday?

Also: we need evidence we can present to our security team: short ops description, where data is stored, and whether ephemeral caches or telemetry are retained. If you can point us to a one-page evidence summary that would help move this along.

Thanks,
Anna Patel
Senior Counsel, Legal & Compliance
ZenHealth Analytics

Attachment: Zen_DPA_Redline_v3.pdf

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Anna Patel <anna.legal@zenhealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-29T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA addendum request: ML model improvement & subprocessor attestations

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear note and the redline. We're aligned on urgency. Short answers up front: yes, we can provide an addendum that includes a no-model-improvement commitment for ZenHealth scope, and yes we can provide a signed attestation for subprocessors.

I'll ask David (Privacy) to surface the operational evidence you can share with procurement/security, and Karthik/Laura from GTM will coordinate timing and any commercial adjustments required for the addendum.

Next steps:
- David: draft a 1-page evidence summary (ephemeral KV behavior, telemetry retention, caching settings, KMS routing).
- Legal (me): draft DPA addendum (we'll use your redline as the baseline) and a short scope sheet for the no-train commitment.
- Ops: provide subprocessor list and attestation template (I'll attach the template).

Attaching our standard attestation template for now: Subprocessor_Attestation_Template.docx. We aim to get a first pass to you by EOD Wednesday. If procurement needs DocuSign, we'll include that link in the next email.

Appreciate the timeline heads-up — will circle back with a draft.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Subprocessor_Attestation_Template.docx

From: Anna Patel <anna.legal@zenhealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@zenhealth.com
Date: 2026-05-30T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA addendum request: ML model improvement & subprocessor attestations

Markus,

Appreciate the quick reply. A couple of clarifications from procurement/security:
- The no-train commitment needs to be scoped to our tenant(s) and state that no transcripts, prompts, or derived embeddings will be used to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any models.
- We will accept a signed attestation from Redwood and from each relevant subprocessor. If a subprocessor refuses to sign, we need to know alternative protective measures.
- The evidence summary should include whether logs or telemetry include prompt text, whether we can opt-out at request level, and whether the KV cache persists beyond the transaction.

If you can include a DocuSign-ready addendum and the signed attestation template, procurement can route for approval quickly.

Thanks,
Anna

Quoted for context:
> On 2026-05-29 Markus Klein wrote:
> > I'll ask David (Privacy) to surface the operational evidence you can share with procurement/security

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Anna Patel <anna.legal@zenhealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-31T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA addendum request: ML model improvement & subprocessor attestations

Hi Anna — David from Privacy here. Thanks for the precise asks; below is a concise operational summary we can share with your security/procurement teams. I'll attach a short evidence pack as well.

Operational evidence summary (one page):
- No-model-improvement (scope): For ZenHealth tenant IDs (to be enumerated in the addendum) we will not use interactions (prompts, transcripts, embeddings, or derived features) to perform model updates, retraining, or evaluation for model improvement. This is enforced at request-routing and capture flags in our serving runtime.
- Data flows & residency: Customer data for ZenHealth will be processed in the US regions only (we will pin to customer-requested regions and document the region IDs in the addendum).
- Cache & telemetry: Session KV caches are ephemeral by default (TTL < 15 minutes) and not persisted to disk. Operational telemetry (request metadata, latency, errors) is collected for service reliability but does not include full prompt text unless debug mode is enabled (debug mode requires customer opt-in and is gated by an internal approval workflow).
- Subprocessors: We will provide the current list of subprocessors and a signed attestation from Redwood that codifies the no-train commitment for your tenant. We will request the same attestation from each relevant subprocessor; if a subprocessor cannot provide a signed attestation, we will either remove them from the processing path for ZenHealth or apply technical compensations (onshore-only processing, additional contract terms, or dedicated routing).

Attached: Redwood_NoTrain_Evidence_Summary.pdf (1p), Subprocessor_Attestation_Template.docx

Mutual action plan (recommended):
1) Redwood legal delivers DPA addendum draft + enumerated tenant IDs (Markus) — target: 2026-06-02 EOD.
2) Redwood ops/infra deliver signed attestation or subprocessor-specific mitigations (David) — target: 2026-06-04.
3) Procurement review & DocuSign (ZenHealth) — target: 2026-06-08.

If useful, we can also propose a short annex that lists the specific API routes and keys that will be excluded from logging/training to make the commitment auditable.

Please let me know if you want additional technical detail for your security checklist.

Regards,
David Kim
Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_NoTrain_Evidence_Summary.pdf, Subprocessor_Attestation_Template.docx

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: DPA addendum request: ML model improvement & subprocessor attestations — next steps

Anna — quick update and plan of record.

1) Draft addendum: I will send a DocuSign-ready DPA addendum that enumerates ZenHealth tenant IDs and includes the explicit no-model-improvement language discussed. Expect that EOD 2026-06-02.
2) Evidence pack: David shared the 1-page summary and the attestation template; we'll collect signatures from subprocessors and surface any gaps.
3) Commercial impact: Karthik/Laura — can you confirm whether the addendum triggers any pricing or SLA exceptions for this account so procurement has complete context?

If procurement is ready to accept the addendum once we have subprocessor attestations, we can move to DocuSign the same day.

Marking this high priority on our side.

Thanks,
Markus
